passages.text: Iolaus: I hold this true, and long have held: Nature hath made one man upright for his neighbours’ good, while another hath a disposition wholly given over to gain, useless alike to the state and difficult to have dealings with,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: but for himself the best of men; and this I know, not from mere hearsay. I, for instance, from pure regard and reverence for my kith and kin, though I might have lived at peace in Argos, alone of all my race shared with Heracles his labours, while he was yet with us, and now that he dwells in heaven,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: I keep these his children safe beneath my wing, though myself I need protection. For when their father passed from earth away, Eurystheus would first of all have slain us, but we escaped. And though our home is lost, our life was saved. But in exile we wander from city to city,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: ever forced to roam. For, added to our former wrongs, Eurystheus thought it fit to put this further outrage upon us: wheresoe’er he heard that we were settling, thither would he send heralds
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: demanding our surrender and driving us from thence, holding out this threat, that Argos is no mean city to make a friend or foe, and furthermore pointing to his own prosperity. So they, seeing how weak my means, and these little ones left without a father,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: bow to his superior might and drive us from their land. And I share the exile of these children, and help them bear their evil lot by my sympathy, loth to betray them, lest someone say, Look you! now that the children’s sire is dead,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus no more protects them, kinsman though he is. Not one corner left us in the whole of Hellas, we are come to Marathon and its neighbouring land, and here we sit as suppliants at the altars of the gods, and pray their aid; for ’tis said
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: two sons of Theseus dwell upon these plains, the lot of their inheritance, scions of Pandion’s stock, related to these children; this the reason we have come on this our way to the borders of glorious Athens. To lead the flight two aged guides are we;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: my care is centred on these boys, while she, I mean Alcmena, clasps her son’s daughter in her arms, and bears her for safety within this shrine, for we shrink from letting tender maidens come anigh the crowd or stand as suppliants at the altar.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Now Hyllus and the elder of his brethren are seeking some place for us to find a refuge, if we are driven by force from this land.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: O children, children, come hither! hold unto my robe; for lo! I see a herald coming towards us from Eurystheus,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: by whom we are persecuted, wanderers excluded from every land. A curse on thee and him that sent thee, hateful wretch! for that same tongue of thine hath oft announced its master’s evil hests to these children’s noble sire as well.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: Doubtless thy folly lets thee think this is a good position to have taken up, and that thou art come to a city that will help thee. No ! there is none that will prefer thy feeble arm to the might of Eurystheus. Begone! why take this trouble? Thou must arise and go
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to Argos, where awaits thee death by stoning.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Not so, for the god’s altar will protect me, and this land of freedom, wherein we have set foot.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: Wilt give me the trouble of laying hands on thee?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: By force at least shalt thou never drag these children hence.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: That shalt thou soon learn; it seems thou wert a poor prophet, after all, in this. [Copreus here seizes the children.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: This shall never happen while I live.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: Begone! for I will take them hence, for all thy refusals, for I hold that they belong to Eurystheus, as they do indeed.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Help, ye who long nave had your home in Athens!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: we suppliants at Zeus’ altar in your market-place are being haled by force away, our sacred wreaths defiled, shame to your city, to the gods dishonour.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Hark, hark! What cry is this that rises near the altar? At once explain the nature of the trouble.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: See this aged frame hurled in its feebleness upon the ground! Woe is me!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Who threw thee down thus pitiably?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Behold the man who flouts your gods, kind sirs, and tries by force to drag me from my seat before the altar of Zeus.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: From what land, old stranger, art thou come to this confederate state of four cities? or have ye left Euboea’s cliffs, and, with the oar that sweeps the sea, put in here from across the firth?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Sirs, no island life I lead,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: but from Mycenae to thy land I come.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: What do they call thee, aged sir, those folk in Mycenae?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Maybe ye have heard of Iolaus, the comrade of Heracles, for he was not unknown to fame.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Yea, I have heard of him in bygone days; but tell me, whose are the tender boys thou bearest in thine arms?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: These, sirs, are the sons of Heracles, come as suppliants to you and your city.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: What is their quest? Are they anxious, tell me, to obtain an audience of the state?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: That so they may escape surrender, nor be tom with violence from thy altars, and brought to Argos.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: Nay, this will nowise satisfy thy masters,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: who o’er thee have a right, and so have tracked thee hither.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Stranger, ’tis but right we should reverence the gods’ suppliants, suffering none with violent hand to make them leave the altars, for that will dread Justice ne’er permit.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: Do thou then drive these subjects of Eurystheus forth, and this hand of mine shall abstain from violence.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: ’Twere impious for the state to neglect the suppliant stranger’s prayer.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: Yet ’tis well to keep clear of troubles,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: by adopting that counsel, which is the wiser.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Thou then, shouldst have told the monarch of this land thy errand before being so bold, out of regard to his country’s freedom, instead of trying to drag strangers by force from the altars of the gods.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: Who is monarch of this land and state?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Demophon, son of gallant Theseus.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: Surely it were most to the purpose to discuss this matter somewhat with him; all else has been said in vain.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Lo! here he comes in person, in hot haste, and Acamas his brother, to hear what thou hast to say.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: Since thou for all thy years hast outstripped younger men in coming to the rescue to this altar of Zeus, do thou tell me what hath chanced to bring this crowd together.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: There sit the sons of Heracles as suppliants, having wreathed the altar, as thou seest, O king,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and with them is Iolaus, trusty comrade of their sire.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: Why should this event have called for cries of pain?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: (turning to Copreus). This fellow caused the uproar by trying to drag them forcibly from this altar, and he tripped up the old man, till my tears for pity flowed.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: Hellenic dress and fashion in his robes doth he no doubt adopt, but deeds like these betray the barbarian. Thou, sirrah, tell me straight the country whence thou earnest thither.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: An Argive I; since that thou seek’st to know.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Who sent me, and the object of my coming, will I freely tell. Eurystheus, king of Mycenae, sends me hither to fetch these back; and I have come, sir stranger, with just grounds in plenty, alike for speech or action. An Argive myself, Argives I come to fetch,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: taking with me these runaways from my native city, on whom the doom of death was passed by our laws there; and we have a right, since we rule our city independently, to ratify its sentences. And though they have come as suppliants to the altars of numerous others,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: we have taken our stand on these same arguments, and no one has ventured to bring upon himself evils of his own getting. But they have come hither, either because they perceived some folly in thee, or, in their perplexity, staking all on one risky throw to win or lose;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: for surely they do not suppose that thou, if so thou hast thy senses still, and only thou, in all the breadth of Hellas they have traversed, wilt pity their foolish troubles. Come now, put argument against argument: what will be thy gain, suppose thou admit them to thy land, or let us take them hence?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: From us these benefits are thine to win: this city can secure as friends Argos, with its far-reaching arm, and Eurystheus’ might complete; whilst if thou lend an ear to their piteous pleading and grow soft, the matter
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: must result in trial of arms; for be sure we shall not yield this struggle without appealing to the sword. What pretext wilt thou urge? Of what domains art thou robbed that thou shouldst take and wage war with the Tirynthian Argives? What kind of allies art thou aiding? For whom
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: will they have fallen whom thou buriest? Surely thou wilt get an evil name from the citizens, if for the sake of an old man with one foot in the grave, a mere shadow I may say, and for these children, thou wilt plunge into troublous waters. The best thou canst say is, that thou wilt find in them a hope, and nothing more;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and yet this falls far short of the present need; for these would be but a poor match for Argives even when fully armed and in their prime, if haply that raises thy spirits; moreover, the time ’twixt now and then is long, wherein ye may be blotted out. Nay, hearken to me;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: give me naught, but let me take mine own, and so gain Mycenae; but forbear to act now, as is your Athenian way, and take the weaker side, when it is in thy power to choose the stronger as thy friends.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Who can decide a cause or ascertain its merits,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: till from both sides he clearly learn what they would say?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: O king, in thy land I start with this advantage, the right to hear and speak in turn, and none, ere that, will drive me hence as elsewhere they would. ’Twixt us and him is naught in common,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: for we no longer have aught to do with Argos since that decree was passed, but we are exiles from our native land; how then can he justly drag us back as subjects of Mycenae, seeing that they have banished us? For we are strangers.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Or do ye claim that every exile from Argos is exiled from the bounds of Hellas? Not from Athens surely; for ne’er will she for fear of Argos drive the children of Heracles from her land. Here is no Trachis, not at all; no! nor that Achaean town, whence thou, defying justice,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: but boasting of the might of Argos in the very words thou now art using, didst drive the suppliants from their station at the altar. If this shall be, and they thy words approve, why then I trow this is no more Athens, the home of freedom. Nay, but I know the temper and nature of these citizens;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: they would rather die, for honour ranks before mere life with men of worth. Enough of Athens! for excessive praise is apt to breed disgust; and oft ere now I have myself felt vexed at praise that knows no bounds.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: But to thee, as ruler of this land, I fain would show the reason why thou art bound to save these children. Pittheus was the son of Pelops; from him sprung Aethra, and from her Theseus thy sire was born. And now will I trace back these children’s lineage for thee.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Heracles was son of Zeus and Alcmena; Alcmena sprang from Pelops’ daughter; therefore thy father and their father would be the sons of first cousins. Thus then art thou to them related, O Demophon, but thy just debt to them beyond the ties of kinship
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: do I now declare to thee; for I assert, in days gone by, I was with Theseus on the ship, as their father’s squire, when they went to fetch that girdle fraught with death; yea, and from Hades’ murky dungeons did Heracles bring thy father up; as all Hellas doth attest.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Wherefore in return they crave this boon of thee, that they be not surrendered up nor torn by force from the altars of thy gods and cast forth from the land. For this were shame on thee, and hurtful likewise in thy state, should suppliants, exiles,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: kith and kin of thine, be haled away by force. For pity’s sake! cast one glance at them. I do entreat thee, laying my suppliant bough upon thee, by thy hands and beard, slight not the sons of Heracles, now that thou hast them in thy power to help. Show thyself their kinsman and their friend;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: be to them father, brother, lord; for better each and all of these than to fall beneath the Argives’ hand.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: O king, I pity them, hearing their sad lot Now more than ever do I see noble birth o’ercome by fortune; for these, though sprung from a noble sire,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: are suffering what they ne’er deserved.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: Three aspects of the case constrain me, Iolaus, not to spurn the guests thou bringest; first and foremost, there is Zeus, at whose altar thou art seated with these tender children gathered round thee;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: next come ties of kin, and the debt I owe to treat them kindly for their father’s sake; and last, mine honour, which before all I must regard; for if I permit this altar to be violently despoiled by stranger hands, men will think
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: the land I inhabit is free no more, and that through fear I have surrendered suppliants to Argives, and this comes nigh to make one hang oneself. Would that thou hadst come under a luckier star! yet, as it is, fear not that any man shall tear thee and these children from the altar by force.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Get thee (to Copreus) to Argos and tell Eurystheus so; yea and more, if he have any charge against these strangers, he shall have justice; but never shalt thou drag them hence.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: Not even if I have right upon my side and prove my case?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: How can it be right to drag the suppliant away by force?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: Well, mine is the disgrace; no harm will come to thee.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: Tis harm to me, if I let them be haled away by thee.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: Banish them thyself, and then will I take them from elsewhere.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: Nature made thee a fool, to think thou knowest better than the god.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: It seems then evildoers are to find a refuge here.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: A temple of the gods is an asylum open to the world.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: Maybe they will not take this view in Mycensa.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: What! am I not lord of this domain?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: So long as thou injure not the Argives, and if wise, thou wilt not.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: Be injured for all I care, provided I sin not against the gods.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: I would not have thee come to blows with Argos.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: I am of like mind in this; but I will not dismiss these from my protection.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: For all that, I shall take and drag my own away.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: Why then perhaps thou wilt find a difficulty in returning to Argos.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: That shall I soon find out by making the attempt.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: Touch them and thou shalt rue it, and that without delay.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: I conjure thee, never dare to strike a herald.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: Strike I will, unless that herald learn discretion.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Depart; and thou, O king, touch him not.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Copreus: I go; for ’tis feeble fighting with a single arm.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: But I will come again, bringing hither a host of Argive troops, spearmen clad in bronze; for countless warriors are awaiting my return, and king Eurystheus in person at their head; anxiously he waits the issue here on the borders of Alcathous’ realm.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: And when he hears thy haughty answer, he will burst upon thee, and thy citizens, on this land and all that grows therein; for all in vain should we possess such hosts of picked young troops in Argos, should we forbear to punish thee. [Exit Copreus.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: Perdition seize thee ! I am not afraid of thy Argos.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Be very sure thou shalt not drag these suppliants hence by force, to my shame; for I hold not this city subject unto Argos, but independently.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: ’Tis time to use our forethought, ere the host of Argos approach our frontier,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: for exceeding fierce are the warriors of Mycenae, and in the present case still more than heretofore. For all heralds observe this custom, to exaggerate what happened twofold. Bethink thee what a tale he will tell his master
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: of his dreadful treatment, how he came very near losing his life altogether.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Children have no fairer prize than this, the being born of a good and noble sire, and the power to wed from noble families; but whoso is enslaved by passion
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and makes a lowborn match, I cannot praise for leaving to his children a legacy of shame, to gratify himself. For noble birth offers a stouter resistance to adversity than base parentage; we, for instance, in the last extremity of woe, have found friends
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and kinsmen here, the only champions of these children through all the length and breadth of this Hellenic world. Give, children, give to them your hand, and they the same to you; draw near to them. Ah! children, we have made trial of our friends,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and if ever ye see the path that leads you back to your native land, and possess your home and the honours of your father, count them ever as your friends and saviours, and never lift against their land the foeman’s spear, in memory of this, but hold this city
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: first midst those ye love. Yea, they well deserve your warm regard, in that they have shifted from our shoulders to their own the enmity of so mighty a land as Argos and its people, though they saw we were vagabonds and beggars; still they did not give us up nor drive us forth.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: So while I live, and after death,—come when it will,—loudly will I sing thy praise, good friend, and will extol thee as I stand at Theseus’ side, and cheer his heart, as I tell how thou didst give kind welcome and protection to the sons of Heracles, and how nobly
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: thou dost preserve thy father’s fame through the length of Hellas, and hast not fallen from the high estate, to which thy father brought thee, a lot which few others can boast; for ’mongst the many wilt thou find one maybe, that is not degenerate from his sire.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: This land is ever ready
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: in an honest cause to aid the helpless. Wherefore ere now it hath endured troubles numberless for friends, and now in this I see a struggle nigh at hand.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: Thou hast spoken well, and I feel confident their conduct will be such; our kindness will they not forget.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Now will I muster the citizens and set them in array, that I may receive Mycenae’s host with serried ranks. But first will I send scouts to meet them, lest they fall upon me unawares; for at Argos every man is prompt to answer to the call,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and I will assemble prophets and ordain a sacrifice. But do thou leave the altar of Zeus and go with the children into the house; for there are those, who will care for thee, even though I be abroad. Enter then my house, old man.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: I will not leave the altar. Let
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: us sit here still, praying for the city’s fair success, and when thou hast made a glorious end of this struggle, will we go unto the house; nor are the gods who champion us weaker than the gods of Argos, O king; Hera, wife of Zeus, is their leader;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Athena ours. And this I say is an omen of success, that we have the stronger deity, for Pallas will not brook defeat. [Exit Demophon.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Though loud thy boasts, there be others care no more for thee for that,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: O stranger from the land of Argos; nor wilt thou scare my soul with swelling words. Not yet be this the fate of mighty Athens, beauteous town!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: But thou art void of sense, and so is he, who lords it o’er Argos, the son of Sthenelus,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: —thou that comest to another state, in no wise weaker than Argos,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and, stranger that thou art, wouldst drag away by force suppliants of the gods, wanderers that cling to my land for help, refusing to yield to our king, nor yet having any honest plea to urge. How can such conduct count as honourable,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: at least in wise men’s judgment?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: I am for peace myself; yet I tell thee, wicked king, although thou come unto my city, thou shalt not get so easily what thou expectest.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Thou art not the only man to wield a sword or targe with plates of brass. Nay, thou eager warrior, I warn thee, bring not war’s alarms against our lovely
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: town; restrain thyself.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: My son, why, prithee, art thou returned with that anxious look? Hast thou news of the enemy? Are they coming, are they here, or what thy tidings? For of a surety yon herald will not play us false.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: No! sure I am their captain, prosperous heretofore, will come, with thoughts exceeding proud against Athens. But Zeus doth punish overweening pride.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: The host of Argos is come, and Eurystheus its king;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: my own eyes saw him, for the man who thinks he knows good generalship must see the foe not by messengers alone. As yet, however, he hath not sent his host into the plain, but, camped upon a rocky brow,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: is watching—I only tell thee what I think this means—to see by which road to lead his army hither without fighting, and how to take up a safe position in this land. However, all my plans are by this time carefully laid; the city is under arms, the victims
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: stand ready to be slain to every god, whose due this is; my seers have filled the town with sacrifices, to turn the foe to flight and keep our country safe. All those who chant prophetic words have I assembled, and have examined ancient oracles, both public and secret,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: as means to save this city. And though the several answers differ in many points, yet in one is the sentiment of all clearly the same; they bid me sacrifice to Demeter’s daughter some maiden from a noble father sprung.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Now I, though in your cause I am as zealous as thou seest, yet will not slay my child, nor will I compel any of my subjects to do so against his will; for who of his own will doth harbour such an evil thought as to yield with his own hands the child he loves?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: And now thou mayest see angry gatherings, where some declare, ’tis right to stand by suppliant strangers, while others charge me with folly; but if I do this deed, a civil war is then and there on foot.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Do thou then look to this and help to find a way to save yourselves and this country without causing me to be slandered by the citizens. For I am no despot like a barbarian monarch; but provided I do what is just, just will my treatment be.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Can it be that heaven forbids this city to help strangers, when it hath the will and longing so to do?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: My children, we are even as those mariners, who have escaped the storm’s relentless rage, and have the land almost within their reach, but after all are driven back from shore by tempests to the deep again.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Even so we, just as we reach the shore in seeming safety, are being thrust back from this land. Ah me! Why, cruel hope, didst thou then cheer my heart, though thou didst not mean to make the boon complete?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: The king may well be pardoned, if he will not slay his subjects’ children; and with my treatment here I am content; if indeed ’tis heaven’s will, I thus should fare, still is my gratitude to thee in no wise lost. Children, I know not what to do for you.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Whither shall we turn? for what god’s altar have we left uncrowned? to what fenced city have we failed to go? Ruin and surrender are our instant lot, poor children! If I must die, ’tis naught to me, save that thereby I give those foes of mine some cause for joy.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: But you, children, I lament and pity, and that aged mother of your sire, Alcmena. Ah, woe is thee for thy long span of life! and woe is me for all my idle toil! ’Twas after all our destined doom to fall into the hands of our hated foe,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and die a death of shame and misery. But lend me thine aid, thou knowest how; for all hope of these children’s safety has not yet left me. Give me up instead of them to the Argives, O king; run no risk, but let me save
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: the children; to love my life becomes me not; let it pass. Me will Eurystheus be most glad to take and treat despitefully, as I was Heracles’ companion; for the man is but a boor; wherefore wise men ought to pray to get a wise man for their foe, and not a proud senseless fool;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: for so, even if by fortune flouted, one would meet with much consideration.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Old man, blame not this city; for though perhaps a gain to us, yet would it be a foul reproach that we betrayed strangers.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: A generous scheme is thine, but impossible.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: ’Tis not in quest of thee yon king comes marching hither; what would Eurystheus gain by the death of one so old? Nay, ’tis these children’s blood he wants. For there is danger to a foe in the youthful scions of a noble race, whose memory dwells upon their father’s wrongs;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: all this Eurystheus must foresee. But if thou hast any scheme besides, that better suits the time, be ready with it, for, since I heard that oracle, I am at a loss and full of fear. [Exit Demophon.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Macaria: Sirs, impute not boldness to me, because
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: I venture forth; this shall be my first request, for a woman’s fairest crown is this, to practise silence and discretion, and abide at home in peace. But when I heard thy lamentations, Iolaus, I came forth, albeit I was not appointed to take the lead in my family.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Still in some sense am I fit to do so, for these my brothers are my chiefest care, and I fain would ask, as touching myself, whether some new trouble, added to the former woes, is gnawing at thy heart.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: My daughter, ’tis nothing new that I should praise thee, as I justly may,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: above all the children of Heracles. Our house seemed to be prospering, when back it fell again into a hopeless state; for the king declares the prophets signify that he must order the sacrifice, not of bull or heifer, but of some tender maid
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: of noble lineage, if we and this city are to exist. Herein is our perplexity; the king refuses either to sacrifice his own or any other’s child. Wherefore, though he use not terms express, yet doth he hint,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: that, unless we find some way out of this perplexity, we must seek some other land, for he this country fain would save.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Macaria: Are these indeed the terms on which our safety depends?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Yea, on these; if, that is, we are successful otherwise.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Macaria: No longer then cower before the hated Argive spear; for I, of my own free will, or ever they bid me, am ready to die and offer myself as a victim. For what excuse have we, if, while this city deems it right to incur a great danger on our behalf,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: we, though we might save ourselves, fly from death, by foisting our trouble on others? No! indeed, ’twere surely most ridiculous to sit and mourn as suppliants of the gods, and show ourselves but cowards, children as we are of that illustrious sire.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Where among the brave is such conduct seen? Better, I suppose, this city should be taken and I (which Heaven forefend!) fall into the hands of the enemy, and then, for all I am my noble father’s child, meet an awful doom, and face the Death-god none the less.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Shall I wander as an exile from this land? Shall I not feel shame then, when someone says, as say they will, Why are ye come hither with suppliant boughs, loving your lives too well? Begone from our land! for we will not succour cowards.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Nay, if these be slain and I alone be saved, I have no hope in any wise of being happy, though many ere now have in this hope betrayed their friends. For who will care to wed a lonely maid or make me mother of his children?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: ’Tis better I should die than meet such treatment, little as I merit it. This were fitter treatment for some other, one that is not born to fame as I am. Conduct me to the scene of death, crown me with garlands, and begin the rites, if so it please you;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: then be victorious o’er the foe, for here I offer my life freely and without constraint, and for my brothers and myself I undertake to die. For I, by loving not my life too well, have found a treasure very fair, a glorious means to leave it.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Ah, what shall I say on hearing the maid’s brave words, she that is ready to die for her brothers? Who can speak more noble words or do more noble deeds henceforth for ever?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Daughter, thou art his own true child, no other man’s but Heracles’,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: that godlike soul; proud am I of thy words, though I sorrow for thy lot. Yet will I propose a fairer method: ’tis right to summon hither all the sisters of this maiden,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and then let her, on whom the lot shall fall, die for her family; for that thou shouldst die without the lot is not just.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Macaria: My death shall no chance lot decide; there is no graciousness in that; peace! old friend. But if ye accept and will avail you
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: of my readiness, freely do I offer my life for these, and without constraint.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Ah, this is even nobler than thy former word; that was matchless, but thou dost now surpass
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: thy bravery and noble speech. I cannot bid, will not forbid thy dying, Omy daughter! for by thy death thou dost thy brothers serve.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Macaria: A cautious bidding thine! Fear not to take a stain of guilt from me; only let me die as one whose death is free.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Follow me, old friend, for in thy arms I fain would die; stand by and veil my body with my robe, for I will go even to the dreadful doom of sacrifice, seeing whose daughter I avow myself.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: I cannot stand by and see thee bleed.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Macaria: At least do thou beg me this boon of the king, that I may breathe out my life in women’s arms instead of men’s.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Demophon: It shall be so, unhappy maid; for this were shame to me to refuse thee honour due, for many reasons: because thou hast a soul so brave; because
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: ’tis right; and thou hast shown more courage than any of thy sex my eyes have ever seen. Now, if thou hast aught to say to these children or thy aged guide, oh ! say the last thou hast to say—then go.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Macaria: Farewell, old friend, farewell! and prithee teach
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: these children to be like thyself, wise at every point; let them strive no further, for that will suffice them. And seek to save them from death, even as thou art anxious to do; thy children are we, thy care it was that nurtured us. Thou seest how I yield my bridal
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: bloom to die for them. For you, my brothers gathered here, may you be happy! and may every blessing be yours, for the which my blood shall pay the price! Honour this old friend, and her that is within the house,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena, the aged mother of my sire, and these strangers too. And if ever heaven for you devise release from trouble and a return to your home, remember the burial due to her that saved you, a funeral fair as I deserve; for I have not failed,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: but stood by you, and died to save my race. This shall be my pearl of price instead of children, and for the maiden life I leave, if there be really aught beyond the grave—God grant there may not be! For if, e’en there, we who are to die shall find a life of care,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: I know not whither one shall turn; for death is held a sovereign cure for every ill.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Maiden of heroic soul, transcending all thy race, be sure the fame that thou shalt win from us, in life, in death, shall leave the rest of women far behind;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: farewell to thee! I dare not say harsh words of her to whom thou art devoted, the goddess-daughter of Demeter. [Exit Macaria.] Children, I am undone, grief unnerves my limbs; take hold and support me to a seat hard by, when ye have drawn my mantle o’er my face, my sons.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: For I am grieved at what hath happened, and yet, were it not fulfilled, we could not live; thus were the mischief worse, though this is grief enough.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Without the will of heaven none is blest, none curst, I do maintain;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: nor doth the same house for ever tread the path of bliss; for one kind of fortune follows hard upon another; one man it brings to naught from his high estate, another though of no account it crowns with happiness.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: To shun what fate decrees, is no wise permitted; none by cunning shall thrust it from him; but he, who vainly would do so, shall have unceasing trouble.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Then fall not prostrate thou, but bear what heaven sends, and set a limit
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to thy soul’s grief; for she, poor maid! in dying for her brothers and this land, hath won a glorious death, and splendid fame shall be her meed from all mankind;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: for virtue’s path leads through troublous ways. Worthy of her father, worthy of her noble birth is this conduct. And if thou dost honour the virtuous dead, I share with thee that sentiment.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): All hail, ye children! Where is aged Iolaus? where the mother of your sire, absent from their place at this altar?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Here am I, so far as I can be present at all.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Why dost thou lie there? Why that downcast look?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: There is come a sorrow on my house, whereby I am distressed.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Arise, lift up thy head.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: I am old, and all my strength is gone.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): But I come with tidings of great joy for thee.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Who art thou? Where have I met thee? I have no remembrance.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): I am a vassal of Hyllus; dost not recognize me now?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Best of friends, art thou come to save us twain from hurt?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Assuredly; and moreover thou art lucky in the present case.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Alcmena, mother of a noble son, to thee I call! come forth, hear this welcome news. For long has anguish caused thee inwardly to waste, wondering if those,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: who now are here, would ever come.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: What means that shout, that echoes throughout the house? Hath there come yet a herald from Argos, O Iolaus, and is he treating thee with violence? Feeble is any strength of mine; yet thus much let me tell thee, stranger,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: never, whilst I live, shalt thou drag them hence. Shouldst thou succeed, no more let me be thought the mother of that hero. And if thou lay a finger on them, thou wilt struggle to thy shame with two aged foes.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Courage, aged dame, fear not; not from Argos
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: is a herald come, with hostile messages.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: Why then didst raise a cry, fear’s harbinger?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: I called thee to come to me in front of this temple.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: I know not what it means; who is this?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: A messenger who says thy grandson cometh hither.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: All hail to thee for these thy tidings! But why is he not here, where is he? if in this land he hath set foot. What hath happened to keep him from coming hither with thee, to cheer my heart?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): He is posting the army he brought with him, and seeing it marshalled.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: Then have I no concern herein.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Yes, thou hast; though it is my business to inquire into these matters.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): What then wouldst thou learn of these events?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: About how many allies has he with him?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): A numerous force; I cannot otherwise describe the number.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: The leaders of the Athenians know this, I suppose?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): They do; already is their left wing set in array.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Is then the host already armed for battle?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Yea, and already are the victims brought near the ranks.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: About what distance is the Argive host from us?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Near enough for their general to be plainly seen.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: What is he about? marshalling the enemy’s line?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): So we guessed; we could not hear exactly. But I must go, for I would not that my master should engage the foe without me, if I can help it.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: I also will go with thee; for I like thee am minded, so it seems, to be there and help my friends.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): It least of all becomes thee thus to utter words of folly.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Far less to shrink from sharing with my friends the stubborn fight.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Mere looks can wound no one, if the arm do naught.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Why, cannot I smite even through their shields?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Smite perhaps, more likely be smitten thyself.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: No foe will dare to meet me face to face.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Friend, the strength, that erst was thine, is thine no more,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Well, at any rate, I will fight with as many as ever I did.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Small the weight thou canst throw into the balance for thy friends.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Detain me not, when I have girded myself for action.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): The power to act is thine no more, the will maybe is there.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Stay here I will not, say what else thou wilt
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): How shalt thou show thyself before the troops unarmed?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: There be captured arms within this shrine; these will I use, and, if I live, restore; and, if I am slain, the god will not demand them of me back. Go thou within, and from its peg take down a suit of armour and forthwith bring it to me.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: To linger thus at home is infamous, while some go fight, and others out of cowardice remain behind. [Exit Servant.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Not yet hath time laid low thy spirit, ’tis young as ever; but thy body’s strength is gone. Why toil to no purpose?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: ’Twill do thee hurt and benefit our city little. At thy age thou shouldst confess thy error and let impossibilities alone. Thou canst in no way get thy vigour back again.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: What means this mad resolve
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to leave me with my children undefended here?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Men must fight; and thou must look to them.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: And what if thou art slain? what safety shall I find?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Thy son’s surviving children will care for thee.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: Suppose they meet with some reverse? which Heaven forefend!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: These strangers will not give thee up, fear not.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: They are my last and only hope, I have no other.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Zeus too, I feel sure, cares for thy sufferings.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: Ah! of Zeus will I never speak ill, but himself doth know, whether he is just to me.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Lo! here thou seest a full coat of mail; make haste to case thyself therein; for the strife is nigh, and bitterly doth Ares loathe loiterers; but if thou fear the weight of the armour, go for the present without it, and in the ranks
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: do on this gear; meantime will I carry it.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Well said! keep the harness ready to my hand, put a spear within my grasp, and support me on the left side, guiding my steps.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Am I to lead this warrior like a child?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: To save the omen, we must go without stumbling.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Would thy power to act were equal to thy zeal!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Hasten; I shall feel it grievously, if I am too late for the battle.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): ’Tis thou who art slow, not I, though thou fanciest thou art doing wonders.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Dost not mark how swift my steps are hasting?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): I mark more seeming than reality in thy haste.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Thou wilt tell a different tale when thou seest me there.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): What shall I see thee do? I wish thee all success, at any rate.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Thou shalt see me smite some foeman through the shield.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Perhaps, if ever we get there. I have my fears of that.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Iolaus: Ah! would to Heaven that thou, mine arm, e’en as I remember thee in thy lusty youth, when with Heracles thou didst sack Sparta, couldst so champion me to-day! how I would put Eurystheus to flight! since he is too craven to wait the onslaught.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: For prosperity carries with it this error too a reputation for bravery; for we think the prosperous man a master of all knowledge.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: O earth, and moon that shines by night, and dazzling radiance of the god,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: that giveth light to man, bear the tidings to me, shout aloud to heaven for joy, and beside our ruler’s throne, and in the shrine of grey-eyed Athene.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: For my fatherland and home will I soon decide the issue of the strife with the gleaming sword, because I have taken suppliants under my protection.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: ’Tis a fearful thing, that a city
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: prosperous as Mycenae is, one famed for martial prowess, should harbour wrath against my land; still, my countrymen, it were a shameful thing in us to yield up suppliant strangers
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: at the bidding of Argos. Zeus is on my side, I am not afraid; Zeus hath a favour unto me, as is my due; never by me shall gods be thought weaker than mortal men.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: O dread goddess, thine the soil whereon we stand, thine this city, for thou art its mother, queen, and saviour; wherefore turn some other way the impious king, who leadeth a host
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: from Argos with brandished lance against this land; for, such my worth, I little merit exile from my home.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: For thy worship is aye performed with many a sacrifice, and never art thou forgotten as each month draweth to its close,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: when young voices sing and dancers’ music is heard abroad, while on our wind-swept hill goes up the cry of joy to the beat of maidens’ feet by night.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Mistress, the message that I bring is very short
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: for thee to hear and fair for me, who stand before thee, to announce. O’er our foes we are victorious, and trophies are being set up, with panoplies upon them, taken from thy enemies.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: Best of friends! this day hath wrought thy liberty by reason of these tidings.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: But there still remains one anxious thought thou dost not free me from;—a thought of fear;—are those, whose lives I cherish, spared to me?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): They are, and high their fame through all the army spreads.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: The old man Iolaus,—is he yet alive?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): Aye, that he is, a hero whom the gods delight to honour.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: How so? Did he perform some deed of prowess?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): He hath passed from age to youth once more.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: Thy tale is passing strange; but first I would that thou shouldst tell me, how our friends won the day.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): One speech of mine puts it all clearly before thee.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: When we had deployed our troops and marshalled them face to face with one another, Hyllus dismounted from his four-horsed chariot and stood midway betwixt the hosts. Then cried he, Captain, who art come from Argos,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: why cannot we leave this land alone? No hurt wilt thou do Mycenae, if of one man thou rob her; come! meet me in single combat, and, if thou slay me, take the children of Heracles away with thee,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: but, if thou fall, leave me to possess my ancestral honours and my home. The host cried yes! saying the scheme he offered was a fair one, both to rid them of their trouble and satisfy their valour. But that other, feeling no shame before those who heard the challenge or at his own cowardice, quailed, general though he was,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: to come within reach of the stubborn spear, showing himself an abject coward; yet with such a spirit he came to enslave the children of Heracles. Then did Hyllus withdraw to his own ranks again, and the prophets seeing that no reconciliation would be effected by single combat,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: began the sacrifice without delay and forthwith let flow from a human throat auspicious streams of blood. And some were mounting chariots, while others couched beneath the shelter of their shields, and the king of the Athenians,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: as a highborn chieftain should, would exhort his host: Fellow-citizens, the land, that feeds you and that gave you birth, demands to-day the help of every man. Likewise Eurystheus besought his allies that they should scorn to sully the feme of Argos and Mycenae.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Anon the Etrurian trumpet sounded loud and clear, and hand to hand they rushed; then think how loudly clashed their ringing shields, what din arose of cries and groans confused! At first the onset of the Argive spearmen
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: broke our ranks; then they in turn gave ground; next, foot to foot and man to man, they fought their stubborn fray, many falling the while. And either chief cheered on his men, Sons of Athens! Ye who till the fields of Argos!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: ward from your land disgrace. Do all we could, and spite of every effort, scarce could we turn the Argive line in flight. When lo! old Iolaus sees Hyllus starting from the ranks, whereon he lifts his hands to him with a prayer
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses
