passages.text: to take him up into his chariot. Thereon he seized the reins and went hard after the horses of Eurystheus. From this point onward must I speak from hearsay, though hitherto as one whose own eyes saw. For as he was crossing Pallene’s hill,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: sacred to the goddess Athene, he caught sight of Eurystheus’ chariot, and prayed to Hebe and to Zeus, that for one single day he might grow young again and wreak his vengeance on his foes. Now must thou hear a wondrous tale: two stars settled on the horses’ yokes
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and threw the chariot into dark shadow, which—at least so say our wiser folk—were thy son and Hebe; and from that murky gloom appeared that aged man in the form of a youth with strong young arms; then by the rocks of Sciron
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: the hero Iolaus o’ertakes Eurystheus’ chariot. And he bound his hands with gyves, and is bringing that chieftain once so prosperous as a trophy hither, whose fortune now doth preach a lesson, clear as day, to all the sons of men,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: that none should envy him, who seems to thrive, until they see his death; for fortune’s moods last but a day.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: O Zeus, who puttest my foes to flight, now may I behold the day that frees me from cruel fear!
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: At last, O Zeus, hast thou turned a favouring eye on my affliction;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: yet do I thank thee for what has happened. And though ere this I did not believe my son was gathered to the gods, now am I convinced thereof. My children, now at last from toil shall ye be free, free from him, whom hideous death awaits,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Eurystheus; now shall ye behold your father’s city, and set foot in the land of your inheritance, and sacrifice to those ancestral gods, from whom ye have been debarred and forced to lead in strangers’ lands a life of wretched vagrancy. But tell me, what sage purpose Iolaus
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: nursed in his heart, that he spared the life of Eurystheus, for to my mind this is no wisdom, to catch a foe and wreak no vengeance on him.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Servant (of Hyllus): ’Twas his regard for thee, that thou might’st see him subject to thy hand, and triumph o’er him.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Rest assured, ’twas no willing prisoner he made, but by strong constraint he bound him, for Eurystheus was loth indeed to come alive into thy presence and pay his penalty. Farewell, my aged mistress; I pray thee remember thy first promise when I was beginning my story;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: set me free; for, at such a time as this, sincerity becometh noble lips. [Exit Servant.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Sweet is the dance to me, whenso the clear-toned flute and lovely Aphrodite shed grace upon the feast;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and a joyful thing too it is, I trow, to witness the good luck of friends, who till then ne’er dreamt of it. For numerous is the offspring of Fate,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: that bringeth all to pass, and of Time, the son of Cronos.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Thine is the path of justice, O my city; this must no man wrest from thee, thy reverence for the gods, and, whoso denieth it of thee, draws nigh to frenzy’s goal,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: with these plain proofs in view. Yea, for the god proclaims it clearly, by cutting short the bad man’s pride in every case.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: In heaven, mother, lives thy son, passed from earth away; that he went down to Hades’ halls, his body burnt by the fire’s fierce flame, is past belief;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: in golden halls reclined he has to wife Hebe, lovely nymph. Thou, O Hymen, hast honoured them, children both of Zeus.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Things for the most part form a single chain;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: for instance, men say Athene used to champion their father, and now the citizens of that goddess have saved his children, and checked the insolence of him, whose heart
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: preferred violence to justice. God save me from such arrogance, such greed of soul! [Eurystheus is brought in bound.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Messenger: Mistress, though thine eyes see him, yet will I announce we have brought Eurystheus hither for thy pleasure,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: an unexpected sight, for him no less a chance he ne’er foresaw; for little he thought of ever falling into thy hands, what time he marched from Mycenae with his toil-worn warriors, to sack Athens, thinking himself far above fortune. But a power
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: divine hath reversed our destinies, changing their position. Now Hyllus and brave Iolaus I left raising an image to Zeus, who routs the foe, for their triumphant victory, whilst they bid me bring this prisoner to thee, wishing to gladden thy heart; for ’tis the sweetest
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: sight to see a foe fall on evil days after prosperity.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: Art come, thou hateful wretch? Hath Justice caught thee then at last? First, turn thy head this way to me, and endure to look thy enemies in the face, for thou art no more the ruler, but the slave.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Art thou the man—for this I fain would learn—who didst presume to heap thy insults on my son, who now is where he is, thou miscreant? What outrage didst thou abstain from putting upon him? Thou that didst make him go down alive even to Hades,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and wouldst send him with an order to slay hydras and lions? Thy other evil schemes I mention not, for to tell them were a tedious task for me. Nor did it content thee to venture thus far only; no! but from all Hellas wouldst thou drive me and my children,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: heaven’s suppliants though we were, grey-heads some of us, and some still tender babes. But here hast thou found men and a free city, that feared not thee. Die in torment must thou, and e’en so wilt thou gain in every way, for one death is not
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: thy due, after all the sorrow thou hast caused.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Messenger: Thou mayst not slay him.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: Then have we taken him captive in vain. But say, what law forbids his death?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Messenger: It is not the will of the rulers of this land.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: Why, what is this? Do they not approve of slaying enemies?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Messenger: Not such as they have taken alive in battle.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: Did Hyllus uphold this decision?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Messenger: He, I suppose, ought to have disobeyed the law of the land.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: The prisoner’s life ought not to have been spared a moment.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Messenger: It was then that he was wronged, by not being slain at first.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: Why, then, he is still in time to pay his penalty.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Messenger: There is no one, who will slay him now.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: I will; and yet I count myself someone.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Messenger: Well, thou wilt incur great blame, if thou do this deed.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: I love this city well; that cannot be gainsaid. But since this man hath fallen into my power, no mortal hand shall wrest him from me. Wherefore let who will, call me the woman bold, with thoughts too high for her sex;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: yet shall this deed be brought to pass by me.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Lady, full well I understand thou hast a dire quarrel with this man, and ’tis pardonable.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Eurystheus: Woman, be sure I will not flatter thee nor say aught to save my life,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: that can give any occasion for a charge of cowardice. It was not of my own free will I took this quarrel up; I am aware that I was born thy cousin, and kinsman to Heracles, thy son; but whether I would or no,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Hera, by her power divine, caused me to be afflicted thus. Still, when I undertook to be his foe, and when I knew I had to enter on this struggle, I set myself to devise trouble in plenty, and oft from time to time my midnight communing bore fruit,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: scheming how to push aside and slay my foes, and for the future divorce myself from fear; for I knew that son of thine was no mere cipher, but a man indeed; yea, for, though he was my foe, I will speak well of him, because he was a man of worth.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Now, after he was taken hence, was I not forced, by reason of these children’s hatred, and because I was conscious of an hereditary feud, to leave no stone unturned by slaying, banishing, and plotting against them? So long as I did so, my safety was assured.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Suppose thyself hadst had my lot, wouldst not thou have set to harassing the lion’s angry whelps, instead of letting them dwell at Argos undisturbed? Thou wilt not persuade us otherwise. Now therefore, since they did not slay me then,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: when I was prepared to die, by the laws of Hellas my death becomes a curse on him, who slays me now. The city wisely let me go, in that she regarded the gods more than her hatred of me. Thou hast had my answer to thy words; henceforth must
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: I be called avenging spirit and noble hero too. ’Tis even thus with me; to die have I no wish, but, if I leave my life, I shall in no way be grieved.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: Alcmena, fain I would advise thee somewhat; let this man go, for ’tis the city’s will.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: Suppose he die, and yet I obey the city?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: That would be best of all; but how can this be?
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: I will teach thee easily. I will slay him and then give up his corpse to those of his friends, who come for it, for, as regards his body, I will not disobey the state;
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: but by his death shall he pay me the penalty.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Eurystheus: Slay me, I do not ask thee for mercy; yet since this city let me go and shrunk from slaying me, I will reward it with an old oracle of Loxias, which in time will benefit them more than doth appear.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Bury my body after death in its destined grave in front of the shrine of the virgin goddess at Pallene. And I will be thy friend and guardian of thy city for ever, where I lie buried in a foreign soil, but a bitter foe to these children’s descendants,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: whensoe’er with gathered host they come against this land, traitors to your kindness now; such are the strangers ye have championed. Why then came I hither, if I knew all this, instead of regarding the god’s oracle? Because I thought, that Hera was mightier far than any oracle,
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: and would not betray me. Waste no drink-offering on my tomb, nor spill the victim’s blood; for I will requite them for my treatment here with a journey they shall rue; and ye shall have double gain from me, for I will help you and harm them by my death.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Alcmena: Why, why delay to kill this man, after hearing this, since this is needed to secure the safety of your city and your children? Himself points out the safest road. Though the man is now our foe, yet after death is he our gain.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Away with him, ye servants, and cast him to the dogs when ye have slain him. Think not thou shalt live to cast me forth from my native land again.
passages.locusKind: TEI line marker; grouped translation text, not independently aligned Greek verses

passages.text: Chorus: I agree. Lead on, servants. Our conduct shall bring no stain of guilt upon our rulers.
